shared_ancestry_rule: FRANK/ClayCode/ClayGraph/UnifiedDB agreement is not counted as independent replication.

reviews.assumption: FRANK architecture relations and invariants require readable relation words to be first-class lexer operators in ClayCode.
reviews.origin: possible inference from current G9/FRANK-readable surface
independent_or_new_evidence: MLIR generic-vs-custom operation syntax as external design triangulation
reviews.reason: Tested binary relation semantics can be represented without granting relation vocabulary lexer/operator status. Readability may remain optional surface sugar.
reviews.counterhypothesis: Declared infix words materially improve model/human reader performance enough to justify a custom surface over the same canonical IR.
reviews.next_test: Matched reader/compiler benchmark over dual surfaces.

reviews.assumption: Parser acceptance of a relation-looking token is sufficient to admit semantic relation identity.
reviews.origin: surface-language risk, not an owner-fixed FRANK law
independent_or_new_evidence: this run 50000-case typed resolver rejection test
reviews.reason: Unknown relation names must fail closed at typed semantic resolution, independently of syntactic acceptance.
reviews.counterhypothesis: A parser can itself be the complete typed resolver with equivalent explicit declaration semantics.

reviews.assumption: One binary Relation representation is sufficient for all FRANK/ClayGraph/Hyperposition relationship semantics.
independent_or_new_evidence: Hyperposition mandatory n-ary identity and pairwise-reduction contract
reviews.reason: Current architecture requires higher-order relation identity and roles; no executable reduction has shown binary equivalence.
reviews.counterhypothesis: Binary graph encoding with auxiliary relation nodes can preserve all semantics at lower complexity.
reviews.next_test: Pairwise/binary reduction versus explicit hyperrelation intervention and replay benchmark.

overall: REFINED: parser surface and semantic relation authority are separated. No FRANK semantic redesign or BASE promotion follows.
